newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to weaker Friday following quiet dealings overnight.

But the precious metals markets were keeping an eye on the dollar which moved sideways to slightly higher overnight, catching its breath after recent gains which, if built on, may prompt further selling in gold, dealers said.
COMEX August gold was called unchanged from Thursday's close of $343.60 an ounce. Bullion was fixed in London this morning at $341.20, a dollar below the Thursday afternoon fix.
Bullion was quoted by dealers at $341.35/85.
COMEX July silver was called flat to off 1.0 cent.
COMEX gold stocks were down 128,792 ounces Thursday while silver stocks fell a sharp 3,536,492 ounces to 198,013,467 ounces.
On ACCESS, August gold last traded at $343.50, off $0.10 from Thursday's close, while July silver was down 1.8 cents at $4.69.
NYMEX July platinum was called $1.00 to $2.00 below Thursday's close of $433.10, with NYMEX September palladium called flat to off $1.00 from Thursday's settlement of $184.25.
Norilsk Nickel said overnight that reduced gas supplies was affecting production of metals.
U.S. producer prices for May, forecast to rise 0.1 percent, were due at 0830 EDT, along with business inventories for April, expected to increase by 0.2 percent.
